decisions.statement: One run goes at a time.
A lock beside the repositories has the run.
A repository already there is left alone.
A repository whose HEAD will not read is cloned again from its mirror.
A repository whose authority is a workstation tree is created empty.
Nothing here takes away a repository that has the only second copy.
A destination and a policy are written on every run rather than only at creation.
A hook is a stub this module writes.
A hook stub runs the script the source cache has.
A step that failed ends the run rather than being passed over.
The folder a hook stub sits in is made before that stub is written.
Whatever a hook's name already reaches is taken away before the stub is written.
A repository repacks on no push.
A repository serves any commit it holds that a branch reaches.

definition: the bare repositories made ready before the transport serves them
